text:
alice: thinking out loud — for the continuous-batcher refactor i sketched last week: what if we introduced a "hybrid spillway" that splits overflow into two lanes: short-deadline fast-evict and long-deadline spill (cold-coalesce)?
ben: sounds promising. curious how we decide deadline vs cost. do you mean per-request deadline hints?
alice: yeah, clients can optionally attach deadline_hint_ms. fallback is based on token-estimate and tenant SLA. goal is avoid evicting tiny low-latency reqs just because a huge batch formed.
claire: one worry: adding lanes increases state and join/leave races. how do we prevent head-of-line blocking when a long request sits in fast lane by mistake?
alice: proposal: admission checks deadline_hint first, then sequence-length-prob, then a quick probabilistic re-route if queue depth > threshold. short lane has strict size cap and preemptible slots.
mark: can we fold this into existing lease model? i.e. treat short-lane slots as preemptible leases with a higher heartbeat freq. if we do that, eviction is just lease revoke.
priya: +1 on using leases. also suggest normalizing eviction score by expected tokens remaining so a 10k token warmup doesn't nukes a 20-token request.
ben: can you show the eviction-score formula you have in mind?
alice: sure — rough: 
```
evict_score = (remaining_tokens * cost_per_token) / max(1, deadline_ms - now_ms)  * tenant_priority_weight
// lower score evicted first
```
claire: meh the division by time gives huge spikes when deadline close. maybe use softplus and clamp: `deadline_factor = 1 / (softplus((deadline_ms-now)/scale))`
alice: good point. scale will need tuning per-hardware-profile. we should keep telemetry counters for "moved-to-spillway" and "preempted-by-lease".
devbot: CI: batcher-unit-tests passed on PR 4823 — flaky test fixed.
mark: ops concern: metrics cardinality explosion if we tag by lane+tenant+model. propose only detailed tags for top 5 tenants, aggregate for the rest.
priya: also add a cheap admission check earlier: if request expected tokens < small_threshold, route straight to fast-path and bypass coalesce entirely. reduces RTT for tiny requests.
ben: rollout strategy? feature-flag per-cluster, with canary on low-traffic rings and a kill-switch to route all to legacy cohort.
alice: yep. will draft RFC follow-up with operator playbook, config knobs: short_lane_size, preempt_heartbeat_ms, softplus_scale, small_threshold, telemetry-sampling.
claire: one more: consider an async fallback where long requests can be polled instead of holding GPU slot — for workloads that accept eventual results. could cut pressure.
alice: nice idea — add `response_mode=async|sync` to the hint set. add it to RFC.
mark: sounds like a plan. i'll schedule a short sync to map the lease changes and telemetry needs.
priya: i'll prepare a simple load-test harness that simulates mixed-length traffic and deadline hints.
alice: thanks all — will follow up with RFC PR and a quick simulation graph. :thumbsup:
